text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you point to exactly where it hurts and tell me how long the pain has been bothering you?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he experience any pain in his left hip, groin, or thigh, especially when you try to rotate his leg inward? I’d also like to check if he has a limited range of motion in that hip.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since knee pain in children is often referred from the hip, I need to examine the hip directly; can you tell me if he has difficulty abducting or internally rotating his left hip? I will also check for any tenderness or crepitus in the hip joint. REQUEST TEST: Pelvic_X-Ray
